summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who has studied algorithms and data structures (divide and conquer, recurrences, sorting, basic complexity), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, binary representation, sets, permutations, induction), and linear algebra (vector spaces, subspaces, dimension, rank, invertible matrices, Gaussian elimination, triangular matrices) at an introductory level. They know the basics of Fourier analysis and probability/real analysis only as far as complex numbers and elementary calculus. They have not studied algebraic number theory, advanced finite-field theory, Lie groups or specialist FFT/multiplication literature.

known.name: Recurrences and divide and conquer
known.gloss: A problem of size N is solved by recursive calls on smaller pieces plus combining work, and the total cost is found by solving the resulting recurrence.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers are identified when they differ by a multiple of a modulus.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and coprime integers share no common factor other than 1.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each one determine a unique residue modulo their product.

known.name: Binary representation and bit operations
known.gloss: Integers are written as strings of bits, with bitwise XOR and carry propagation in addition.

known.name: Radix (base) expansion
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a finite set of positions.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: Sets closed under linear combinations, described by a basis, with dimension the basis size.

known.name: Finite field F_2
known.gloss: The two-element field where addition is XOR and multiplication is AND.

known.name: Matrices, rank and invertibility
known.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices that compose by multiplication; invertible ones have an inverse and rank counts independent rows.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Row operations reduce a matrix to triangular form, giving factorizations into triangular pieces.

known.name: Cartesian product of sets
known.gloss: The set of tuples with each coordinate drawn from its own set, used to index multidimensional arrays.

known.name: Cyclic groups and roots of unity
known.gloss: The integers mod n under addition form a cyclic group, and the n-th roots of unity are the complex solutions of z^n = 1.

known.name: Real and complex analysis basics
known.gloss: Absolute values and norms of real and complex numbers, the triangle inequality, and elementary functions such as exp.

known.name: Rounding, floor and ceiling
known.gloss: Floor, ceiling and nearest-integer maps from reals to integers.

known.name: Logarithms and exponents
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm and the arithmetic of exponents and powers of two.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and Karatsuba
known.gloss: The standard quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication and its divide and conquer speedup.

known.name: Sorting and merging
known.gloss: Ordering records by key, with comparison sorting costing O(N log N).

known.name: Pigeonhole principle and counting arguments
known.gloss: Elementary counting tools for finite sets, subsets and their sizes.

known.name: Lower and upper bound asymptotics
known.gloss: Theta, Omega and little-o relate growth rates of functions alongside big-O.

known.name: Constants and parameters in complexity bounds
known.gloss: Fixed constants hidden in big-O and powers of log n as polylogarithmic factors.
